description: For each real algebraic sampling phase between one and two, the 547/727 and 571/599 races have exactly specified recoverable prime logarithms. At phase 3/2 neither field isolates one prime alone and together they isolate 31 and 47. At every algebraic phase in (97/64, 49/32], the two fields together isolate no prime logarithm. For each odd prime, the transcendental phases where a rational multiple of the specified 547/727 reading recovers its logarithm form a countable dense set. The union of all phases recovering a prime by any finite algebraic combination is countable. All claims are unconditional.
title: Which primes survive a shift of the dyadic sampling grid?
